questions.stem: To which modelling family does Focal Point Data Modelling belong?
options: Ensemble Data Modelling, like Data Vault
Dimensional Modelling, like the star schema
Pre-relational modelling, like the network model
NoSQL modelling
Semantic modelling
questions.explanation: Just like Data Vault, Focal Point Data Modelling belongs to the family of Ensemble Data Modelling.

questions.stem: How many stages, called Focal Forms, make up the Focal modelling process?
options: Three
Five
Six
Ten
Two
questions.explanation: The Focal methodology is organised into five distinct stages referred to as Focal Forms, from identifying business concept entities through to atomic context.

questions.stem: What is done in Focal Form One?
options: Group attributes into Descriptor Concepts
Determine atomic context
Identify and define the primary business concept entities
Identify natural business relationships between concepts
Identify attributes of the core concepts
questions.explanation: Focal Form One identifies and defines the primary business concept entities; relationships, attributes, descriptor grouping and atomic context follow in Forms Two to Five.

questions.stem: What makes Focal Form Four unique to the Focal methodology?
options: It defines the business keys of each entity
It creates the link tables between entities
It historises every attribute by default
It categorises attributes into one of ten predefined Descriptor Concepts, each with a specific definition
It builds the semantic layer
questions.explanation: Focal Form Four groups attributes into one of ten predefined Descriptor Concepts, emphasising good definition practice, which is unique to Focal.

questions.stem: In Focal Point modelling, which example is given of a Condition descriptor in a Loan Focal?
options: The customer's name
The officer's branch
The loan identifier
The payment date
The interest rate, as a financial Condition
questions.explanation: A Condition is a qualifying attribute that constrains or specifies requirements; in a Loan Focal the interest rate is a financial Condition, while a Contract's start date and an Order's payment date are temporal Conditions.

questions.stem: What does Focal Form Five, Atomic Context, determine?
options: Which attributes group together at the most granular level to answer a specific atomic question, usually no more than five related attributes
Which entities are the primary business concepts
Which ten Descriptor Concepts apply
Which relationships are historical
Which fact tables share conformed dimensions
questions.explanation: Atomic Context identifies attribute sets of a small number, usually no more than five, of related attributes at the most granular level, which is crucial for physical implementation.

questions.stem: How does the stability of a Focal Point physical model compare with Data Vault?
options: Focal models evolve more frequently than Data Vault models
Focal physical models typically remain stable with minimal changes, whereas Data Vault physical models tend to evolve more frequently
Both change at the same rate
Neither model can change after implementation
Focal models are regenerated for every load
questions.explanation: Once implemented, a Focal Point physical data model typically remains stable with minimal changes, unlike Data Vault where the physical model evolves more often.

questions.stem: How does historisation in Focal Point modelling differ from Anchor modelling?
options: Focal historises every Descriptor by default; Anchor does not
Focal uses LoadDate only; Anchor uses ValidFrom only
In Focal, historisation is not enforced on every Descriptor, whereas Anchor enforces it
Focal has no temporal capability at all
They are identical
questions.explanation: Focal Descriptors can be temporal with ValidFrom/ValidTo, but unlike Anchor, historisation is not enforced on every Descriptor, giving less rigidity and more business-friendly structures.

questions.stem: In the comparison of dimensional, ensemble and temporal modelling, how is temporal modelling characterised?
options: As a competing family alongside Kimball and ensemble
As a replacement for Data Vault
As a type of snowflake schema
As a cross-cutting principle that elevates time to a first-class citizen and must be applied within relational, dimensional or ensemble structures
As a NoSQL technique
questions.explanation: Temporal modelling is not a schema by itself; it is a design principle that makes time explicit across all entities and relationships and is applied within other structures.

questions.stem: Why is temporal handling in dimensional modelling described as "bolted on"?
options: Because dimensional models cannot store dates
Because fact tables never record time
Because Slowly Changing Dimensions are forbidden
Because dimensional models store history in satellites
Because history is handled partially at attribute level through Slowly Changing Dimensions rather than systemically across every entity and relationship
questions.explanation: In dimensional models time is present through SCD techniques, but it is partial and attribute-level rather than deeply embedded in the model's structure.
